notes: Iter 17 — NEW APPROACH: constructive grower replaces WFC + extend. Algorithm: place STATION_N at origin, push its port to frontier, pop random port, try TEE/CURVE/STRAIGHT/RAMP that matches entry+Y, fall back through the chain. Loop-close via STRAIGHT/CURVE → TEE → CROSS upgrade. Stop when frontier empty. Connectivity guaranteed by construction.

Iter 16: extendWFCLayout missed the parallel-overpass tile decompositions in its layout-build loop (only had under-pass), so when WFC's second pass placed a PARALLEL_OVERPASS_RAMP, the layout kept it as a virtual tile and samplePath threw. Added the three parallel decomp branches.

Iter 15: fixed extendWFCLayout's stacked-cell pin logic — was misidentifying parallel overpasses as under-passes (rotations didn't match the variant), causing 9/10 second-roll solves to throw and fall back to first-roll only. Now distinguishes rotations correctly and pins parallel-overpass / under-pass / transition variants per case.

Iter 14: probe now does the ADDITIVE flow per set — generates baseline layout A, then runs extendWFCLayout(A) to get layout B that 'fits around' A. SVG renders B with roll-2-added cells in yellow-orange so you can see what the second pass contributed. Also re-running dev-server screenshots so trains in PNG ride the additive (extended) layout, not just the first pass.
Iter 13: dropped the redundant elevated-graph JunctionTrack (was duplicating decks at every cell the elevated graph traced through ground level). Visual track duplication should be gone now.

Iter 12: parallel-overpass pillars moved to the SIDES of the track instead of along it, so the lower track passes between them lengthwise (no more pillars sitting on the lower deck). Under-pass cells (perpendicular layers) keep the along-track placement.

Iter 11: Eulerian tour now drives both probes AND actual train logic in main.ts (Hierholzer + greedy odd-pair edge duplication, exposed as TrackGraph.eulerianTour()). Trains visibly walk every edge instead of bouncing between 2 stations.
Iter 10: trains now use Eulerian tour (Hierholzer + greedy odd-pair edge duplication). Visits every graph edge at least once. Expecting coverage to spike toward 100%.

Iter 7: stations bumped 6→20 (cap; layouts typically have fewer STRAIGHT candidates). Hypothesis: cycle visits almost every straight cell, coverage spikes.
